fix: compact-card collapse bug and brighten dark-glass panel text

Root-caused the intermittent "thin strip" bug (title only, description

poster image response and loaded a deep link that auto-selects a
stakeholder on load. The card's height gets measured once during init;

ever re-measures afterward, since only selection changes and window
resize triggered a re-sync. That also explains why it looked
stakeholder- and session-specific rather than a clean repro: a click
on a different stakeholder later in the same session re-measures
correctly, because by then the image has loaded.

trigger list that turned out to be incomplete. Kept an explicit image
load listener alongside it as a fast first sync. This same fix also
resolves the standing "card ends short of its column" backlog item -
same stale-measurement root cause, smaller gap. Raised the minimum-
height safety floor from 60px to 200px regardless of cause.

walkthrough bar, explanation section, and case card (near-white
#E8EDF5, was muted blue-gray) for readability, while leaving section
headings, the reviewed-date note, source lines, and the stakeholder
list's inactive rows at their existing muted tone so the active-row
highlight and heading hierarchy still read clearly. Re-checked WCAG AA
against the worst-case bright-backdrop scenario (~9.5:1, clears AA

head_commit.message:
fix: swipeable sub-layer cards on mobile

The 5-card sub-layer row (#chain) didn't fit 375px screens: min-width
per card forced the whole page into horizontal overflow, dragging the
hero status strip and ticker band along with it even though neither
was independently overflowing.

Fixed with a standard mobile-only horizontal scroll-snap row: 80vw
peek-width cards as the primary swipe cue, a right-edge fade that
hides once scrolled to the end, and the arrow connectors hidden below
768px since they don't fit at that card width. Desktop is untouched.

Found and fixed the same root cause twice while building this:
buildChain() was setting layout properties (card flex/min-width, arrow
display) as inline styles via JS, which silently beats any external
CSS regardless of specificity or media query. Moved the static layout
values into proper CSS rules and kept only the genuinely per-score
dynamic values (colors, conditional glow) inline.

Verified against a real pipeline run with Playwright at 375/414/1400px:
zero horizontal page overflow, exact 80vw card width, fade behavior
correct, expand panel still opens below the row, desktop pixel-
identical before and after. Zero console errors.

  use this map" block and an always-visible, clickable "All stakeholders"
  list (14 entries, TSO/DSO combined) that collapses to a single toggle
  row once a stakeholder is selected, freeing room for its content.
- Replaced a CSS percentage-height chain that didn't reliably resolve
  with a pixel-measured fixed height, so the card always fills its
  column instead of leaving a large gap for short content or clipping
  long content; added a bottom fade + styled scrollbar for the cases
  that still overflow.
- Moved the walkthrough (both paths, Prev/Next, step text) above the
  poster so its highlights land in the same viewport at wide widths,
  and removed the now-duplicate "Currently highlighted" block below.
- Slimmed the hero into a two-row layout, fixed a glow-clipping bug on
  the back-link, and gave the "Static reference" badge a teal outline.
- Found and fixed a first-render timing bug twice (default-state card,
  then independently the walkthrough intro text) — both were a
  hand-rolled opacity+setTimeout fade left unguarded on a cold first
  paint. Consolidated into a single safeFade() helper everything now
  routes through, so a future addition can't reintroduce the same bug
  by hand-rolling the pattern again.

highlight, others dim, side panel populates from the same data. Legend
doubles as a multi-select filter. Hover/focus an edge for a tooltip.

connection & power -> equipment -> customers -> waste heat) with
prev/next. Case card highlights operator+hyperscaler+district_heating+
public_sector+dso+tso together for the real Fortum/Microsoft example.

(same data), not a cramped tiny diagram.

separately in Node: all relationship/walkthrough/case-study stakeholder
